page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.2xlarge is an x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and has a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU hardware.

Benchmark data places this instance consistently in the average performance tier across various compute and memory workloads. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1417.0 and a multi-core score of 5299.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 424.06 GB/sec and a large block write speed of 37.49 GB/sec. For database operations, the instance handles 7.81 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 4027.57 on Passmark database tests.

While the instance performs adequately on standard tasks, it exhibits significant performance limitations on larger computational models. LLM inference speeds for a medium 7B model are poor, yielding only 15.81 tokens/sec for prompt processing and 5.96 tokens/sec for text generation. Consequently, this instance is not suited for complex AI workloads but is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive applications that do not require local storage. It is best suited for relational databases, in-memory caching, web serving, and software compilation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m8.2xlarge is an x86_64 virtual machine instance featuring 8 dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs (4 physical cores) running at 2.5 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, it provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU but lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmark results place the instance in the average tier for general compute, memory bandwidth, and database operations, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 10405.69 and 7.81 million Redis SET operations per second. However, it exhibits poor performance on larger workloads like 7B LLM inference. This memory-optimized profile is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without high-performance storage, making it well-suited for in-memory databases, caching layers, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
